title: SQL catalog
description: The SQL statements a PHP application can issue, as reported by sql-catalog.

$schema.description: Where the schema for this document is written.

version.description: The format version. A reader that does not know this number should not guess.

statements.description: How many statements the catalog holds.

resolved.description: How many of them have no gaps left in their text.

undetermined.description: How many of them still have gaps.

findings.description: How many findings were reported across them.

statements.description: The statements, ordered by where they are issued.

problems.description: Files that could not be analyzed at all.

file.description: The file, relative to the analysis root.

message.description: Why it could not be analyzed.

id.description: The identifier the statement keeps across runs. Built from the file, the enclosing function, the database call and the statement shape, and deliberately not from the line number.

kind.description: What the statement does to the database.

sql.description: The statement text. Every value the analyzer could not pin down is written as {$}.

exact.description: Whether the text holds no gaps.

resolution.description: How far the analyzer got, and why it got no further. `external-input` means the values were followed to runtime input, so the text cannot be fixed; `incomplete-model` means a dependency the analyzer does not model was reached; `incomplete` means a cycle or a budget stopped the search; `not-analyzed` means the call was found but never examined, so no statement was read from it.

searchClosed.description: Whether the analyzer closed every dependency it set out to follow. When false, the statements listed for this call site may not be all of them.

correlated.description: Whether the alternatives at this call site are ones the code can reach. When false, the text was assembled from parts that vary independently, so some listed combinations may be unreachable.

tables.description: The tables the statement names, in order and without repeats.

file.description: The file, relative to the analysis root.

line.description: The line the call is written on.

function.description: The enclosing function, as Class::method, a function name, or {main}.

sink.description: The database call that was matched, such as pdo.prepare. The value `unmatched` means the call is written the way a database call is written but what it is called on could not be worked out.

through.description: The path the analyzer took to this reading, from the body the walk started in to the one holding the call, outermost first.

placeholders.description: The bind parameters, in the order they are written.

findings.description: What is worth reporting about the statement.

token.description: The parameter as written, such as ?, :id or $1.

position.description: The zero-based order of the parameter in the statement.

name.description: The parameter name, for parameters bound by name.

value.description: What the parameter is bound to, or null when no binding was found.

type.description: The static type, written the way PHP writes it.

values.description: The values the parameter can take, when they are all known.

exhaustive.description: Whether `values` is all of them. When false, only `type` is a statement about the value.

origins.description: Where the unresolved parts of the value come from.

origin.description: Where a value the analyzer could not pin down comes from.
